Example: X = no. of heads in 3 coin flips

- `dbinom(x)`: P(X = x)



```{r}
# prob of gettung 2 heads

dbinom(2, 3, 0.5)
choose(3, 2)*(0.5)^2*(1-0.5)^1

dbinom(0:3, 3, 0.5)
```


- `pbinom()`: by default, the prob to the left of a point.

$$P(X \le q) = \sum_{i=0}^q P(X=i)$$

`lower.tail = F` then pbinom gives you the prob to right of a point excluding the point

$$P(X > q) = \sum_{i=q+1}^{\inf} P(X=i)$$

```{r}
# Prob of getting atmost 2 heads. P(X<= 2)

pbinom(2, 3, 0.5) #P(X<= 2) = P(X=0)+P(X=1)+P(X=2)

0.125 + 0.375 + 0.375

sum(dbinom(0:2, 3, 0.5))
```

```{r}
pbinom(2, 3, 0.5, lower.tail = F) # P(X = 3) = P(X>2)

# 0.125 0.375 0.375 0.125 

1 - pbinom(2, 3, 0.5) # same as pbinom(2, 3, 0.5, lower.tail = F). That is lower.tail argument gives you the compliment probability


# Prob of getting atleast 2 heads, P(X >= 2)

pbinom(1, 3, 0.5, lower.tail = F)
```






# Can you have a binomial distribution that starts from 1? No 0 in the sample space.

- `qbinom()`: inverse function of pbinom(), gives the point that covers a certain prob to the left (by default) or the right (if `lower.tail = F` is used).  


```{r}
qbinom(0.5, 3, 0.5)

sum(dbinom(0:1, 3, 0.5))

gbinom(3, 0.5) 
```

```{r}
qbinom(0.7, 3, 0.5) # 70th percentile

sum(dbinom(0:2, 3, 0.5))

qbinom(seq(0.5, 0.90, by = 0.05), 3, 0.5) # qbinom returns 2 for all the percentiles between 50 and 87.5, because X is a discrete variable
```

```{r}
gbinom(20, 0.05)

20*0.05
```

$$n*p*(1-p) \ge 10$$

The center of every normal distribution is controlled by it's expected value or $\mu$.The height of the normal distribution is controlled by it's standard deviation, $\sigma$. The higher the curve, lower is the deviation.
